From 6689f01d6740cf358932b3e97ee968c6099800d9 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Jan Kara <jack@suse.cz>
Date: Mon, 13 Apr 2026 11:36:19 +0200
Subject: [PATCH] writeback: Fix use after free in inode_switch_wbs_work_fn()

inode_switch_wbs_work_fn() has a loop like:

  wb_get(new_wb);
  while (1) {
    list = llist_del_all(&new_wb->switch_wbs_ctxs);
    /* Nothing to do? */
    if (!list)
      break;
    ... process the items ...
  }

Now adding of items to the list looks like:

wb_queue_isw()
  if (llist_add(&isw->list, &wb->switch_wbs_ctxs))
    queue_work(isw_wq, &wb->switch_work);

Because inode_switch_wbs_work_fn() loops when processing isw items, it
can happen that wb->switch_work is pending while wb->switch_wbs_ctxs is
empty. This is a problem because in that case wb can get freed (no isw
items -> no wb reference) while the work is still pending causing
use-after-free issues.

We cannot just fix this by cancelling work when freeing wb because that
could still trigger problematic 0 -> 1 transitions on wb refcount due to
wb_get() in inode_switch_wbs_work_fn(). It could be all handled with
more careful code but that seems unnecessarily complex so let's avoid
that until it is proven that the looping actually brings practical
benefit. Just remove the loop from inode_switch_wbs_work_fn() instead.
That way when wb_queue_isw() queues work, we are guaranteed we have
added the first item to wb->switch_wbs_ctxs and nobody is going to
remove it (and drop the wb reference it holds) until the queued work
runs.

Fixes: e1b849cfa6b6 ("writeback: Avoid contention on wb->list_lock when switching inodes")
CC: stable@vger.kernel.org
Signed-off-by: Jan Kara <jack@suse.cz>
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20260413093618.17244-2-jack@suse.cz
Acked-by: Tejun Heo <tj@kernel.org>
Signed-off-by: Christian Brauner <brauner@kernel.org>

diff --git a/fs/fs-writeback.c b/fs/fs-writeback.c
index 3c75ee025bda..d63baa1b6fec 100644
--- a/fs/fs-writeback.c
+++ b/fs/fs-writeback.c
@@ -570,28 +570,30 @@ void inode_switch_wbs_work_fn(struct work_struct *work)
 	struct inode_switch_wbs_context *isw, *next_isw;
 	struct llist_node *list;
 
+	list = llist_del_all(&new_wb->switch_wbs_ctxs);
 	/*
-	 * Grab out reference to wb so that it cannot get freed under us
+	 * Nothing to do? That would be a problem as references held by isw
+	 * items protect wb from freeing...
+	 */
+	if (WARN_ON_ONCE(!list))
+		return;
+
+	/*
+	 * Grab our reference to wb so that it cannot get freed under us
 	 * after we process all the isw items.
 	 */
 	wb_get(new_wb);
-	while (1) {
-		list = llist_del_all(&new_wb->switch_wbs_ctxs);
-		/* Nothing to do? */
-		if (!list)
-			break;
-		/*
-		 * In addition to synchronizing among switchers, I_WB_SWITCH
-		 * tells the RCU protected stat update paths to grab the i_page
-		 * lock so that stat transfer can synchronize against them.
-		 * Let's continue after I_WB_SWITCH is guaranteed to be
-		 * visible.
-		 */
-		synchronize_rcu();
+	/*
+	 * In addition to synchronizing among switchers, I_WB_SWITCH
+	 * tells the RCU protected stat update paths to grab the i_page
+	 * lock so that stat transfer can synchronize against them.
+	 * Let's continue after I_WB_SWITCH is guaranteed to be
+	 * visible.
+	 */
+	synchronize_rcu();
 
-		llist_for_each_entry_safe(isw, next_isw, list, list)
-			process_inode_switch_wbs(new_wb, isw);
-	}
+	llist_for_each_entry_safe(isw, next_isw, list, list)
+		process_inode_switch_wbs(new_wb, isw);
 	wb_put(new_wb);
 }
 
-- 
2.34.1

## Summary of Modifications

The patch modifies a single file: **fs/fs-writeback.c**. The change is made in the function `inode_switch_wbs_work_fn()`.

### Modifications in `fs/fs-writeback.c`

- **Removed the outer `while (1)` loop** that repeatedly drained and processed `new_wb->switch_wbs_ctxs`.
- **Moved the `llist_del_all()` call** outside the loop, so it is executed only once per work invocation.
- **Added a `WARN_ON_ONCE(!list)` check** to catch an unexpected empty list (indicating a potential bug).
- **Simplified the control flow**: after verifying the list is non‑empty, the function acquires a reference to `new_wb` via `wb_get()`, performs an `synchronize_rcu()`, and then processes all items in the batch exactly once before releasing the reference.
- The logic for processing each inode (`process_inode_switch_wbs`) remains unchanged.

### Relationship Between the Modifications

The key relationship is that **removing the loop prevents a use‑after‑free race condition**. Previously, the loop allowed `wb->switch_wbs_ctxs` to become empty while the work item was still pending. This made it possible for a `wb` to be freed (since no isw items held a reference) before the work function could run, leading to a use‑after‑free when `wb_get(new_wb)` was eventually called. By processing only one batch per work invocation, the patch ensures that whenever work is queued (via `wb_queue_isw()`), the list contains at least one item, which holds a reference to `wb` and prevents premature deallocation. This eliminates the race without requiring more complex synchronization.

Signed-off-by: Jan Kara <jack@suse.cz>
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20260413093618.17244-2-jack@suse.cz

Here is the root cause:
The loop in `inode_switch_wbs_work_fn()` repeatedly drained `wb->switch_wbs_ctxs`, allowing it to become empty while the work item was still pending. This allowed the workqueue to schedule the work again, but without any items in the list, no reference to `wb` was held, leading to a use-after-free when the work function later tried to access `new_wb`.

Here is the patch:
 
 void inode_switch_wbs_work_fn(struct work_struct *work)
 {
 	struct bdi_writeback *new_wb = container_of(work, struct bdi_writeback,
 						    switch_work);
 	struct inode_switch_wbs_context *isw, *next_isw;
 	struct llist_node *list;
 
+	list = llist_del_all(&new_wb->switch_wbs_ctxs);
 	/*
-	 * Grab out reference to wb so that it cannot get freed under us
+	 * Nothing to do? That would be a problem as references held by isw
+	 * items protect wb from freeing...
+	 */
+	if (WARN_ON_ONCE(!list))
+		return;
+
+	/*
+	 * Grab our reference to wb so that it cannot get freed under us
 	 * after we process all the isw items.
 	 */
 	wb_get(new_wb);
-	while (1) {
-		list = llist_del_all(&new_wb->switch_wbs_ctxs);
-		/* Nothing to do? */
-		if (!list)
-			break;
-		/*
-		 * In addition to synchronizing among switchers, I_WB_SWITCH
-		 * tells the RCU protected stat update paths to grab the i_page
-		 * lock so that stat transfer can synchronize against them.
-		 * Let's continue after I_WB_SWITCH is guaranteed to be
-		 * visible.
-		 */
-		synchronize_rcu();
+	/*
+	 * In addition to synchronizing among switchers, I_WB_SWITCH
+	 * tells the RCU protected stat update paths to grab the i_page
+	 * lock so that stat transfer can synchronize against them.
+	 * Let's continue after I_WB_SWITCH is guaranteed to be
+	 * visible.
+	 */
+	synchronize_rcu();
 
-		llist_for_each_entry_safe(isw, next_isw, list, list)
-			process_inode_switch_wbs(new_wb, isw);
-	}
+	llist_for_each_entry_safe(isw, next_isw, list, list)
+		process_inode_switch_wbs(new_wb, isw);
 	wb_put(new_wb);
 }

Reason: The provided code snippet still contains the while loop that repeatedly drains `new_wb->switch_wbs_ctxs`. Although `wb_get(new_wb)` is called at the start, this only protects the wb during the current work invocation. When new isw items are added during processing, they may be drained in the same loop, and the work may be re‑queued. After the loop exits and the current invocation calls `wb_put`, the wb could be freed if no other references exist. The re‑queued work then runs with an empty list (since all items were already processed) and attempts `wb_get(new_wb)` on a freed object, leading to a use‑after‑free. The fix requires removing the while loop so that each work invocation drains the list exactly once and never runs with an empty list, guaranteeing that at least one isw item holds a reference to wb when the work executes.
